summary.en: Model a program as objects that keep related data and actions together.
summary.bn: একই জিনিসের ডেটা আর কাজ এক অবজেক্টে রেখে প্রোগ্রাম সাজাতে শিখুন।

notes: The object model introduced here uses ordinary Java 17 classes.

sections.title: Think in terms of things and responsibilities
From a procedure to a responsible object
Classes, instances and the four pillars

practice.title: Model a library loan
practice.statementHtml: Name the state and behaviour of a library loan; explain why the due date belongs there.
practice.answerHtml: State: book code, borrower roll, due day and returned status. Behaviour: renew, mark returned and ask whether overdue. The due day belongs to this loan because different borrowers can have different deadlines.

practice.title: Find the owner of a rule
practice.statementHtml: A marks register rejects marks outside 0 to 100. Explain where this rule belongs in an object design.
hints: Consider a second screen changing the same mark.
practice.answerHtml: A Result object should control changes to its mark. Its changeMark operation checks the range before saving. A display function may show an error, but it should not be the only place enforcing the rule.

practice.title: Identify four pillars
practice.statementHtml: Use a payment service to explain encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism.
hints: Separate hiding details from sharing a parent type.
practice.answerHtml: Encapsulation protects an account balance. Abstraction exposes pay(amount) without showing storage details. Inheritance can describe a specialised account from a general account. Polymorphism allows different payment types to respond differently to the same pay request.

practice.title: Choose a design
practice.statementHtml: Compare a one-use arithmetic calculation with a growing library system and recommend a design for each.
hints: Count independent kinds of state before choosing classes.
practice.answerHtml: A small function is enough for one arithmetic calculation. A library system benefits from Book, Member and Loan objects because their rules and states change independently. OOP adds structure, but the extra structure should solve a real maintenance problem.

quiz.prompt: Which fact is state in a Student object?
options: The act of printing a report
quiz.explanation: A mark describes the student now. Printing is behaviour, while the compiler is a separate tool.

quiz.prompt: What does a class describe before you create any students?
options: The fields and operations shared by student objects
The machine address of every student
quiz.explanation: A class gives a common shape. Individual objects hold individual values.

quiz.prompt: Two books have the same title; why can they still be different objects?
options: They can represent separate physical copies
quiz.explanation: Identity distinguishes copies even when some state matches.

quiz.prompt: Which design puts a balance rule closest to its data?
options: A print function repairs all balances
quiz.explanation: Account operations can guard every balance change. A comment cannot enforce a rule.

quiz.prompt: A caller uses borrowBook without seeing storage details; which pillar is most directly illustrated?
quiz.explanation: Abstraction exposes a useful operation while hiding how the work is organised.

quiz.prompt: Which relationship is a reasonable candidate for inheritance?
quiz.explanation: Inheritance models an is-a relationship. Owning something is a has-a relationship.

quiz.prompt: Different notification objects respond to send; what idea does this preview?
quiz.explanation: The same operation can produce behaviour suited to each object type.

quiz.prompt: How does procedural thinking usually organise a small marks program?
options: Around functions that process mark data
quiz.explanation: Procedural design emphasises the steps and functions. It can still use structured data.

quiz.prompt: Why is Java useful when learning object design?
options: Its class and type rules make object relationships explicit
It removes the need for algorithms
It makes every value an object
quiz.explanation: Java has explicit class rules, but primitive values are not objects and algorithms still matter.

quiz.prompt: When should you add a class to a small calculation?
options: When it gives related state and rules a useful home
quiz.explanation: A class should express a responsibility. Extra classes alone do not improve speed or clarity.

keyPoints.en: An object has identity, state and behaviour.
keyPoints.bn: অবজেক্টের নিজস্ব পরিচয়, বর্তমান অবস্থা আর কাজ থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A class describes the structure of its objects.
keyPoints.bn: ক্লাস বলে দেয় তার অবজেক্টে কী ডেটা আর কাজ থাকবে।

keyPoints.en: Procedural design groups work around functions.
keyPoints.bn: প্রসিডিউরাল ডিজাইনে ফাংশনকে ঘিরে কাজ সাজানো হয়।

keyPoints.en: Encapsulation keeps rules close to the data they protect.
keyPoints.bn: এনক্যাপসুলেশন ডেটার পাশে তার নিয়ম রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Abstraction lets callers focus on useful operations.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যাবস্ট্রাকশন দিয়ে ব্যবহারকারী দরকারি কাজের দিকেই মন দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Inheritance and polymorphism support related types with different behaviour.
keyPoints.bn: ইনহেরিট্যান্স আর পলিমরফিজম সম্পর্কযুক্ত টাইপের ভিন্ন কাজ বোঝাতে সাহায্য করে।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish a class from an object using a library example.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Book is a class describing fields such as code and title. Two Book objects can represent two copies with different codes. The class defines the shape; each object has its own identity and state.

examQuestions.question: Propose three classes for a course registration system and assign one rule to each.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Student holds a roll and checks an allowed credit limit. Course holds its code and capacity. Registration links a student to a course and rejects a duplicate enrollment. Keep each rule with the state needed to enforce it.

examQuestions.question: Explain the four pillars without claiming that every program needs inheritance.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Encapsulation protects data through operations. Abstraction presents essential operations. Inheritance specialises a parent type. Polymorphism lets a common operation vary by object type. Small designs can use the first two without introducing a class hierarchy.
